To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the Shull et al. model provides a good fit to the data for both pigeons and rats and (2) a nonlinear least-squareds data-reduction technique is an efficient and effective method to fit the model.
the Shull et al. model can be extended to include a refractory period and a banded distribution of interresponse times, both extensions being analytically tractable.

the Shull et al. model can be expressed in an analytic form, that the analytic form can be used to fit experimental data to estimate the parameters of the model, that the analytic expression can be used in Monte Carlo simulations of interresponse time distributions, and that the analytic form is easily extended to incorporate refractory period and strongly-banded responding.
